title: Shortest Subarray With a Large Sum (Negative Numbers Allowed)

concept.title: Prefix sums and a deque of candidate starts
body: With only positive numbers, a sliding window with two pointers finds the shortest subarray whose sum is at least `k`. With **negative** numbers the window method breaks: a longer window may have a smaller sum, so you cannot decide whether to shrink or to grow. Use **prefix sums** `P[0..n]` (`P[0] = 0`, `P[i] = a[0] + ... + a[i-1]`): the subarray `a[x..y-1]` has the sum `P[y] - P[x]`. We want the closest pair `x < y` with `P[y] - P[x] >= k`.

Keep a **deque of indexes** `x` whose prefix sums are **increasing**. For a new end `y`: (1) while the front `x` satisfies `P[y] - P[x] >= k`, record the length `y - x` and **remove the front**: any later end would only give a longer subarray for this start. (2) While the back has `P[back] >= P[y]`, **remove the back**: `y` is a later start with a smaller or equal prefix sum, which is always better than the back one. (3) Push `y` at the back.
Every index enters and leaves the deque once: O(n). The prefix sums can exceed 32 bits (`20000 * 10^5`), so use 64-bit integers in C++ and Java.

statement: Given `n` integers (they may be negative) and a number `k`, find the length of the shortest non-empty contiguous subarray whose sum is at least `k`. Print `-1` if there is no such subarray.

examples.note: The subarray 2 3 has the sum 5 and the length 2. No single number reaches 4.
No subarray has a sum of at least 5: the answer is -1.

hints: Two pointers do not work with negative numbers. Work with prefix sums.
Keep a deque of start indexes with increasing prefix sums.
Remove from the front when the sum is reached, and from the back when the new prefix sum is not larger.

explanation: A deque keeps start indexes with increasing prefix sums. When the front start reaches the sum k it is recorded and removed; starts with a prefix sum not smaller than the new one are removed from the back.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

from collections import deque

prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
for i in range(n):
    prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + a[i]
dq = deque()
best = n + 1
for i in range(n + 1):
    while dq and prefix[i] - prefix[dq[0]] >= k:
        best = min(best, i - dq.popleft())
    while dq and prefix[dq[-1]] >= prefix[i]:
        dq.pop()
    dq.append(i)
print(best if best <= n else -1)
